rationale: CheckRun 02a227375cd64387a032521091c09d94 returned completed/tests_passed with exit 0, 17 parsed CA_EVENT observations and 0 parsing errors; indices 0-15 reproduce probes A-C unchanged, and index 16 is the sweep summary for the revision that adds configuration changes: seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=467, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=317, violations=0. That index is the receipt for the configuration-change half of the open gap (984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2), so I interpret it here as a holds-only result over this wider event set, while recording that the set is still narrower than the gap names: the configuration events were single ChangeNodes on node 4 (learner add, voter add, remove) applied through applyConfChange, not joint transitions or learner promotions of an existing voter, node 4 was represented by the package's black-hole stepper so it never participated in any decision, and restarts from persisted storage are still absent. The gap therefore stays open, and no experiment is requested this turn.

interpretations.rationale: Index 16 shows the sweep with configuration changes admitted into the event stream: 317 conf-change proposals were actually issued (against 452 ordinary proposals and 467 elections) and the four invariants still reported violations=0, so the receipt contains no witness for at-most-one-leader-per-term, committed (index, term) divergence, committed-index regression, or applied > committed once nodes apply committed conf changes through applyConfChange. This is the first receipt whose event set reaches the mechanism the suspicion named - support counted while the tracked configuration changes - because the earlier revision applied no configuration at all. The absence is still bounded: the changes are single-node Changes on node 4 only, so no joint configuration and no promotion/demotion of an existing voter was exercised, node 4 never responded (black-hole stepper) so every committed decision rested on the original three voters, and restarts from persisted storage are missing entirely. Two construction facts from this revision belong in the record: messages addressed to a configured-but-absent node crash the repository's network helper (raft_test.go:4117 dereferences a missing state machine), and only registering the package's own black-hole stepper for that id makes configuration events safe to run; consequently the receipt's configuration coverage is real but does not include a newly configured node that participates. The conclusion is therefore holds-only for this event set, with the defect claim refuted only in the narrow sense that no witness appeared.
counterevidence: Only single-node changes on node 4 were proposed, so the joint-consensus decision path (both halves of a joint quorum) was not part of the event stream even though the gap names it.
Node 4 never processed a message, so configuration changes altered quorums and progress tracking without ever testing whether a freshly added participant can vote, be promoted, or be snapshotted.

The sweep's own limits persist: checking happens between events rather than during delivery, committed entries are compared by term at an index rather than full identity, and application is modelled by nextEnts on every step so the applied index never trails committed by more than one event.
limitations: Zero violations over 60 fixed seeds with 317 configuration events is not a rate bound and says nothing about seeds or event orders outside this set.

The harness registers a black-hole peer for the configured id, which is the repository's own test facility but not a real participant; a faithful configuration case needs a state machine that actually responds.
No requirement or comparison anchors were declared, so the receipt carries parsed events only and its meaning rests on this interpretation.
